structure.heading: Technical Debt Inventory and 90-Day Continuous Improvement Roadmap to Improve Lead Time and MTTR
text_content: **Technical Debt Inventory and 90-Day Continuous Improvement Roadmap to Improve Lead Time and MTTR**

Total quantified technical debt is 420 engineer-hours as of 30-06-2026. This inventory was compiled from GitHub issue tags, Jira debt tickets, and CI analytics across the delivery organization. The top debt driver is CI flakiness at 110 engineer-hours across 23 flaky tests. Other contributors include legacy library updates, 85 engineer-hours; insufficient observability, 70 engineer-hours; code duplication hotspots, 55 engineer-hours; environment setup and documentation, 40 engineer-hours; and security rule tuning, 60 engineer-hours. The inventory is validated by engineering leads and recorded in the debt register for executive review.

Remediation prioritization ranks items by risk, cost to fix, and expected lead time impact; CI flakiness is highest priority. Action items include: 1. Stabilize flaky tests, triage 23 tests, add flaky-test decorators and retry policies (estimated 70 engineer-hours). 2. Observability improvements, implement distributed tracing and service-level dashboards (estimated 50 engineer-hours). 3. Dependency upgrades, staged library updates with canary releases, 85 engineer-hours. Owners: Platform SRE, Core Services, and Release Engineering. Expected outcome: fewer pipeline retries, reduced false failures, and faster PR merge cycles.
2026. Governance: monthly steering review with Platform SRE, Product Engineering, and Release Engineering owners; executive briefing.

structure.heading: Q1–Q2 2026 DORA Metrics Baseline and Performance Gaps for the Software Delivery Pipeline
text_content: **Q1–Q2 2026 DORA Metrics Baseline and Performance Gaps for the Sotfware Delivery Pipeline**

During the baseline window (2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31) and the comparison window (2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30) we collected the DORA metrics for the software delievry pipeline across Engineering and Platform teams. Baseline measurements established initial values for deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, and MTTR to enable direct quarter-over-quarter comparison and to focus remediation on process and tooling gaps.
week throughput while monitoring queue times and observability trends.

Change failure rate decreased from 18% in Q1 2026 to 12% in Q2 2026, a six-percentage-point improvement and a 33% relative reduction in failed deployments. This decline reduced incident volume and correlated with improved service stability. Priorities now include consolidating post-deployment monitoring, expanding automated rollbacks, and refining rnubook effectiveness to sustain lower failure rates while tracking MTTR and lead-time metrics at release boundaries.
